items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was that Willy Jones by any chance? [INTERVIEWEE] No, No I know Willy Jones, no. I'm not going to call this boy's name.

ctx.x: a lot of drummers, they'll sit down, they don't think. They're putting a good support behind your solo in good rhythm, they think that they aren't doing anything and so they'll start doing their little thing behind your solo. Here's a funny story. Lester Young was going into the Birdland, so it was a time that I had a studio there in New York, Walter Thomas and I. This is before Gene Krupa. So Pres wanted a drummer and I had a very good drummer up there, at least he was good on the pad and could read, fast hands…
Was that Willy Jones by any chance?

No, No I know Willy Jones, no. I'm not going to call this boy's name. So anyway Pres says, okay, Cozy, and Pres did keep him, kept him there for his run at Birdland, but the first night, he went down there and this boy was up there, dropping bombs ... and Pres up there trying to take a solo you know, so Pres waited until the whole set was over and Pres went over to him and said, 'Pops,' he says, 'man, you're up there just playing your buns off. But behind my solos, just give me a little titty-boom, titty-boom,…
